images.caption: Figure 1:PixelOne-Pro on the accuracy–latency frontier.The main plot compares mean accuracy and latency across four benchmarks. The ScreenSpot Pro and OSWorld-G insets each compare both Pro models with the four highest-scoring external GUI-specialized baselines. The leaderboard bars use a truncated linear accuracy scale from 50% to 80%. Full results and timing details appear inTable1andSectionS4.4.

Figure 2:From spatial search to single-forward grounding.(a) The teacher scores row and column choices with VideoJEV’s native head. (b) The teacher refines candidate regions through zoomed search. (c) The student inherits the teacher’s shared parameters and learns from its spatial distributions to predict a click with one visual encoding and one model forward.

Figure 3:One decision head, two kinds of options.(a) The teacher uses the native decision head to score text options. (b) PixelOne reuses this head to select a visual token and adds a pixel head to locate the click within it.

Figure 4:Direct pixel prediction alongside teacher search.PixelOne-Pro-35B-A3B locates the shown ScreenSpot Pro targets in a single forward pass. Across the full benchmark, it correctly localizes 230 targets missed by T3.SectionS5.3provides further analysis.

Figure S2:Single-forward grounding across four benchmarks.In all sixteen selected cases, four per benchmark, PixelOne-Pro-4B succeeds and same-scale T3 and AR fail. Columns show ScreenSpot, V2, Pro, and OSWorld-G. Crops are for display only. Boxes mark targets, and border arrows indicate predictions outside the crop.

Figure S4:Successful grounding on lower-resolution screenshots.These four original screenshots have a long side of at most 1,600 pixels. The top row shows the full screenshot with the display crop outlined. Subsequent rows show saved predictions on the same crop at the same scale within each column. Pink boxes denote targets, and mouse-pointer tips denote predictions. PixelOne-Pro pointers are blue, and baseline pointers are gray. Hit and Miss indicate the original point-in-box outcomes. All displayed predictions lie within their crops.

Figure S5:Successful grounding on higher-resolution screenshots.Comparisons follow the column layout and visual conventions ofFigureS4. Original image sizes range from2,560×1,4402{,}560\times 1{,}440to5,120×1,4405{,}120\times 1{,}440. Each model receives the same original screenshot and instruction through its evaluated input pipeline. Crops are for display only. These selected examples illustrate differences in click placement. Aggregate accuracy is reported in the main results.

Figure S6:Token selection followed by within-token pixel selection.The first column overlays full-image token probabilities and circles the selected-token location for visibility. The second enlarges that token and its immediate neighbors. Gray grid lines mark token boundaries, and a dashed outline marks the selected token. The third shows saved pixel probabilities within that32×3232\times 32token. The last column marks the final click with a blue mouse pointer. Pink boxes are ground truth, not model inputs. Probability maps are normalized independently for display with their maxima labeled. Click coordinates are in original-image pixels.
